input.quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the date and year first above written and shall continue in operation for at least an initial period of twenty-five (25) years following the RFS Date (hereinafter referred to as "initial Period") and shall be terminable thereafter by agreement of the Parties. However, any Party may terminate its participation in this Agreement at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter by giving not less than one (1) year's prior notice thereof, in writing, to the other Parties.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no auto-renewal mechanic at all: there is no fixed renewal term, no "unless either party gives notice" roll-over, and no renewal price-uplift language anywhere in the document (searches for "renew", "automatically" and "prior notice" return only §18). After the 25-year Initial Period the Agreement simply continues in operation and, critically, we hold a unilateral, unconditional right under §18.1 to exit at the end of the Initial Period or at any time thereafter — we are never locked into a further multi-year term, so the walk-away trigger (automatic multi-year renewals) is not engaged, and the pricing concern behind the rule does not arise because ongoing charges are cost-shared O&M under §§6-7 rather than a vendor-set renewal price. The only feature short of the preferred position is the one (1) year exit notice, which is longer than the 30/60-day windows the playbook contemplates; we note it but do not redline it: it is mutual and symmetrical (it equally guarantees us twelve months' warning of any other Party's withdrawal), it reflects the operational reality of a jointly owned submarine cable system, and §18.4 further protects a withdrawing Terminal Party by requiring the remaining Parties to negotiate continued operation of its Terminal Station. Substantively this sits at or above the fallback and a shortened window would be disproportionate to the consortium bargain.
